# Tinted page ground

<!-- Generated by php artisan standards:install from tey/standards; do not edit. -->

Rule ui.surface-on-tinted-ground (warn only). A theme whose page ground is tinted declares it with one token, --kit-ground: tinted, in its own resources/css. On it the content sits on cards and the page chrome stays on the ground; from tey/kit 0.15.27 the kit's DataTable, EmptyState, Workbench and PageSection draw that card themselves, and FormCard is a card on any ground.

No generator yet; follow the summary and stamp the file `standards-pattern: ui-page.tinted-ground`.

Kit: @kit/ui Page, @kit/ui DataTable, @kit/ui FormCard, @kit/ui EmptyState, @kit/ui Card.
Checks: ui.surface-on-tinted-ground. Run `php artisan standards:check --changed` before committing.

Conventions:
- Declare a tinted ground with --kit-ground: tinted on :root in the app's own CSS, next to the colours: the ground (--background, or --shell-ground for the shell alone) and a lighter --card. A white ground declares nothing.
- On a tinted ground, content sits on a card (bg-card text-card-foreground border rounded-xl, as a dashboard widget): the kit's DataTable, EmptyState, Workbench and PageSection content draw it from tey/kit 0.15.27, and FormCard and the form Section are cards already. Never a card inside a card.
- Page, PageGrid and the page chrome stay on the ground: the page header, breadcrumbs, SubNav, tabs and section headings. PageSection surface="none" leaves a section's content on the ground.
- A raw <table> or <form> is never a direct child of Page, PageGrid or PageGridItem on a tinted ground: use DataTable or FormCard, or put it in a Card or a PageSection. On a kit before 0.15.27 a DataTable there needs a card too.
- Contrast on a tinted ground: --card against the ground at least 1.1:1 with a --border edge, --border against --card at least 1.5:1, --input against --card at least 3:1, and --foreground and --muted-foreground at least 4.5:1 on the ground and on the card (tey/kit's test:token-contrast).

Related: `ui-page.layout-rhythm`, `ui-page.styling`.

Graduates: To a ready leaf when a second app adopts a tinted ground and the kit's minimums are checked from the app (kit:status).

Not sure this is the right leaf? It answers "Styling, or page layout?" Call bakery.find, or run `php artisan standards:pattern --recipe=ui-page.tinted-ground` to see its siblings.
